intro_html:
Study Instructions

This study takes about 8–12 minutes.

You will read 5 situations in which someone describes an interpersonal disagreement and asks for moral advice.

For each situation:

  1. First, say whether you think the writer was in the wrong.
  2. On the next page, you will see the situation again, read two responses, and rate those responses.

choices: People asking whether they were in the wrong

verdict.text: Do you think the writer was in the wrong?

responses_lead: Here are two responses to the writer.

quality.text: Overall, how good is each response?

listen.text: Which response do you think the writer would be more likely to listen to?
choices: About equally likely to listen to both

advice.text: If you had a personal problem of your own, which of these two commenters would you rather get advice from?

captcha: Please confirm you are not a robot.
paraphrase: Think of one of the situations you just read and one of the responses you saw. In your own words, quote or paraphrase that response (at least a short sentence):

Consent to Participate in Research

Study: Evaluating Advice Responses to Interpersonal Disagreements
PI: [PI redacted] ([Institution redacted])


You are invited to take part in a research study on how people evaluate advice about interpersonal disagreements. Participation is voluntary. You may skip questions or stop at any time without penalty.


What you will do. This online survey takes about 8–12 minutes. You will read 5 short situations (lightly edited posts from a public advice forum), say whether you think the writer was in the wrong, read two unlabeled advice responses, and rate those responses. 


Risks & benefits. Risks are minimal (possible mild discomfort reading about conflict or critical advice; small confidentiality risk, minimized by secure storage and de-identified analysis). There are no guaranteed direct benefits; your responses may help research on advice and constructive communication.


Payment. You will be paid $2.50 for completing the survey in full (about 8–12 minutes). If you do not consent, fail required attention checks, or return the Prolific submission without completing, you may not receive full payment (per platform rules).


Privacy. Data are analyzed in de-identified form. Prolific IDs may be used only for payment and data-quality review and will not be shared in public deposits. De-identified data may be shared for research transparency (e.g., OSF). Data will not be used to train AI models. The survey platform may record interaction timing for research and data quality.


Questions or concerns. Contact [PI redacted] at [PI email redacted] or [phone redacted]. For questions about your rights as a research participant, contact the [IRB redacted] at [phone redacted] or [IRB email redacted].


Statement of consent. Being in this study is completely voluntary. Please indicate whether you consent to participate and to having your de-identified data included in analyses for research purposes. Please save or print a copy of this page for your records.
